detail: BLUEPRINT SECTION 11 DISCREPANCY 1. Section 11 lists 'defensive contribution now pays forwards' as a difference from 2025/26. FALSE. Forwards were eligible from the 2025/26 LAUNCH at the same 12 CBIRT threshold -- the PL's own 2025/26 changes article states midfielders AND forwards need 12 including ball recoveries. The 2026/27 article frames the mechanic as 'remaining', not being extended. Downstream consequence: the 2025-26 calibration season ALREADY CONTAINS forward DC observations under the exact 2026/27 rule; no FWD-specific extrapolation is needed and any scope premised on FWD DC being unobserved is unnecessary.

source: project's own in-store measurement (data-requirements.md P2, 2026-08-21) + vaastav DATA_DICTIONARY.md fetched 2026-08-22 + data-sources.md 1.2 element_stats
detail: BLUEPRINT SECTION 11 DISCREPANCY 2, and the one that unblocks the task. Section 11 says recoveries are 'unobtainable per-player-per-match from every affordable source surveyed'. That is true ONLY of seasons before 2025-26. FPL is an Opta customer and publishes 'recoveries', 'tackles', 'clearances_blocks_interceptions' and 'defensive_contribution' PER PLAYER PER FIXTURE, FREE, in its own public API (element-summary history; mirrored in vaastav gw*.csv). The project already MEASURED this: 29,338 rows for 2025-26, uniformly zero for every earlier season. The blocker is therefore HISTORICAL DEPTH (pre-2025-26), not observability -- a different and much smaller problem. Grain is per FIXTURE not per gameweek, so DGW aggregation before threshold application would silently corrupt double gameweeks. Caveat: no 2026/27 per-match row exists yet anywhere (GW1 being played 22-23 Aug); the live-season 'yes' is a strong inference from element_stats, and becomes an observation only after GW1 settles.

DC THRESHOLDS (10 and 12) ARE PRESS-ONLY. game_config.scoring.defensive_contribution publishes the POINTS (2) and nothing about the required COUNT. The 10/12 values rest entirely on premierleague.com editorial, not on any machine-readable surface. TIME-CRITICAL: event/1/live/ 'explain' blocks after GW1 settles (from Mon 24 Aug local) will pin both thresholds by observation for the first time this season and remove the last press-only dependency in the entire rule set. Also unverifiable by me: whether any event 'overrides' block could alter DC -- no reporting found, cannot rule out.

source: Fantasy Football Scout 2026-02-23 'Opta's new ball recovery definition: What does it mean for FPL?'; Opta/Stats Perform event definitions
detail: Opta REWORDED the ball-recovery definition in FEBRUARY 2026 -- mid-2025/26 season, i.e. inside the single calibration season. Old wording emphasised the ball being 'played directly to him by an opponent'; new emphasises 'full control must be established'. FFS reports the impact as clarificatory only, not a collection change and not retroactive. GOOD NEWS FOR CALIBRATION: had it been a real collection change the one calibration season would have been split across two incompatible definitions. Tiered MEDIUM not HIGH -- it rests on one specialist outlet's characterisation of Opta's intent, not an Opta statement read directly. If DC work ever surfaces an unexplained mid-2025-26 level shift in recoveries, this is the first hypothesis to test.

source: secondary reporting of sports-reference.com blog 2026-01 (primary 403s to this agent); The IX Sports; community aggregation
detail: FBREF LOST ALL OPTA ADVANCED STATS ON 2026-01-20. Stats Perform terminated the Sports Reference agreement and required immediate removal, reportedly eight days after being named FIFA's exclusive betting-data distributor for the 2026 World Cup. Historical pages reportedly remain but no longer update. Relevant because FBref's 'Recov' field (Miscellaneous Stats) was the one free public per-player recoveries surface outside FPL. It is not a live option now, and pre-2022 FBref data is StatsBomb-era, a different provider definition again. The project already had FBref dead on a Cloudflare 403; the underlying reason is now more fundamental and should not be re-litigated. Tiered MEDIUM because the primary announcement could not be read.

PROXY VERDICT: no proxy is needed for ANY season the model is scored on (2026/27 observed live; 2025-26 observed and in-store). For pre-2025-26 backfill a proxy is possible but section 11's 'player season rate x team per-match total' shape will get the MEAN roughly right and the thing that PAYS wrong, because DC is a THRESHOLD statistic -- what matters is P(CBIRT >= 12), governed by per-match DISPERSION, and the estimator carries no information about a player's own dispersion (it inherits the TEAM's, a different quantity). Two players with identical 8.0 CBIRT/90 season rates but different match-to-match variance have very different DC yields and the estimator cannot distinguish them. Second problem: components are POSITIVELY CORRELATED within a match (a pinned-back team produces more of everything simultaneously), so modelling components separately and summing understates the upper tail -- exactly where DC points live. Third: no 60-minute qualifier and no pro-rating, so the minutes distribution interacts multiplicatively and is first-order. VERDICT: a proxy is defensible ONLY if fitted on 2025-26 and validated against THRESHOLD-CROSSING accuracy, never against rate accuracy. If that validation is skipped, anyone claiming the proxy is good IS guessing, and the guess is structurally biased in the direction that matters.

RECOMMENDATION AGAINST PRE-2025-26 BACKFILL. One season of FPL-native ground truth is ~380 matches / 29,338 player-match rows -- not a small dataset for a per-match count model with strong positional and team-style structure. A multi-season backfill buys rows measured under a DIFFERENT PROVIDER'S DEFINITIONS for a rule that pays on FPL's counters specifically, and that definitional bias is unmeasured except in 2025-26, the one season you would not need it for. More decisively, the dominant error in a 2026/27 DC forecast is not sampling noise from one season, it is ROLE AND SYSTEM CHURN -- and extra seasons of a player's history do not help when what changed is his manager or his team's possession share. Investment in team-style conditioning will outperform investment in historical depth, free, at lower risk of silent definitional bias. Offered as judgement, not fact.

source: premierleague.com 'Who's best at earning defensive contribution points in Fantasy?' pub 2026-07-30 (2025/26 data)
detail: ARCHETYPES DC ACTUALLY PAYS. Of the ten highest DC earners in 2025/26, FIVE WERE CENTRE-BACKS AND FIVE WERE DEFENSIVE MIDFIELDERS. Nothing else. (1) CB at a deep-block low-possession side is the best profile in the game -- no recoveries needed (10 CBIT) and the role mechanically generates clearances: Senesi 67.6% hit rate / 50 DC pts / 11.5 DC per 90, Mavropanos 66.7%/36, C.Hughes 63.9%/46, Hill 63.6%/28, Andersen 60.6%/40, Tarkowski 59.5%/44, Egan 57.1%/48, Lacroix 57.1%/40, O'Shea 56.5%/52. (2) Single-pivot ball-winner at a low-possession side: E.Anderson 70.3%/52 (highest of any player any position), Matusiwa 56.8%/50, Garner 52.6%/40. (3) FORWARDS ESSENTIALLY NEVER -- eligible since day one, ZERO in the 2025/26 top ten; 12 CBIRT is not repeatably reachable from a front line. Treat FWD DC as a near-zero term with occasional outliers, NOT a modelling target. (4) Full-backs weaker than intuition: they press and tackle well but as DEFENDERS get NO recovery credit and their clearance volume is far below a CB's. (5) GOALKEEPERS: DC scoring is 0 yet keepers post the HIGHEST recoveries per 90 in the league (Roefs 10/90, Martinez 8.7/90) -- any pipeline computing DC without a position gate will put keepers top of a worthless leaderboard. DC is NOT a minor term: 50-52 points for the best specialists is roughly a quarter to a third of a good defender's season total.

source: nottinghamforest.co.uk 2026-07-02 + mancity.com (both clubs); tottenhamhotspur.com; Sky Sports; ESPN
detail: THE ROLE-VS-NUMBERS DIVERGENCE, most decision-relevant item this pass. ELLIOT ANDERSON HAS JOINED MANCHESTER CITY FROM NOTTINGHAM FOREST for a reported 116m, five-year deal, club record and reported British record -- confirmed by BOTH CLUBS. Anderson was the best DC player in the league (70.3% hit rate, 52 DC pts, and per Opta Analyst 2025-11-28 EIGHT-POINT-ONE-SEVEN ball recoveries per 90, the ONLY OUTFIELD PLAYER IN THE LEAGUE'S TOP 19 on that metric). That profile is a property of FOREST'S SYSTEM, NOT OF ANDERSON. Recoveries and CBIT are out-of-possession counters generated by NOT HAVING THE BALL; Man City are the most possession-dominant side in the division. Any model carrying his 2025/26 per-90 DC rate forward will rank him the premier DC midfielder in FPL and he may not clear the threshold half as often. Same logic, LESS SEVERELY, for MARCOS SENESI (Bournemouth -> TOTTENHAM, free transfer, officially joined 2026-07-01 on contract expiry, De Zerbi's second signing after Andy Robertson, confirmed by tottenhamhotspur.com): top-rated DC defender moving from a mid-block to a side that will hold materially more of the ball; smaller downgrade because CBIT is less possession-elastic than recoveries and Spurs are not City. GENERALISABLE RULE: DC IS A TEAM-STYLE STATISTIC WEARING A PLAYER'S NAME. The strongest predictor of DC yield is how LITTLE of the ball a player's team has, filtered through whether his role puts him in the defensive third; player identity is the SECOND input, not the first. A DC model conditioning on player history alone will be systematically wrong for every player who moved across the possession spectrum -- and MOST CONFIDENTLY wrong about the highest-profile ones, because they are the ones who move.

MIRROR CASE. Promoted for 2026/27: COVENTRY (champions), IPSWICH (2nd), HULL (play-off final, 1-0 v Middlesbrough). Charlie Hughes and John Egan (Hull) and Dara O'Shea and Azor Matusiwa (Ipswich) carry top-tier 2025/26 DC numbers into the PL at circa 4.0-5.0m prices. Their DC rate should be revised UP relative to a naive Championship-to-PL translation, because they will have LESS of the ball in the Premier League than in the Championship -- the opposite direction to the usual promoted-player downgrade. Two real cautions: a Championship CBIT rate is not a PL CBIT rate, and promoted-side defenders carry high minutes risk from squad churn. No study quantifying the translation was found.

task: DC rules verification, observability survey, proxy verdict, archetypes
summary: Wrote docs/wiki/defensive-contribution.md. TWO BLUEPRINT SECTION 11 DISCREPANCIES, both escalated as findings, neither edited by me (blueprint is Architect-only). (1) 'DC now pays forwards' is false -- forwards eligible since the 2025/26 launch at the same 12 CBIRT (premierleague.com 2025-08-10, HIGH). (2) 'Recoveries unobtainable per-player-per-match from every affordable source' is false for 2025-26 and the live season -- FPL's own API publishes recoveries per player PER FIXTURE, free, and the project has already measured 29,338 such rows in-store. The estimator is far less blocked than recorded: the gap is historical depth pre-2025-26, not observability. Rules verified unchanged for 2026/27 (DEF 10 CBIT, MID+FWD 12 CBIRT, 2 pts, capped) but the THRESHOLDS remain press-only and absent from the API -- pinnable empirically from event/1/live explain once GW1 settles, flagged time-critical. Proxy verdict: none needed for any season that will be scored; for pre-2025-26 a proxy is defensible only if validated against threshold-crossing accuracy rather than rate accuracy, and I recommend AGAINST the backfill entirely because role/system churn dominates sampling noise. Archetypes: deep-block CBs and low-possession single-pivot DMs, five and five of the 2025/26 top ten, nothing else; forwards essentially never; keepers score zero DC but top the recoveries table, so a position gate is mandatory. Headline football finding: DC is a team-style statistic wearing a player's name -- Elliot Anderson, the league's best DC player, has moved to Manchester City for a club-record fee (both clubs confirm), and Senesi to Tottenham; carrying their 2025/26 rates forward would be badly wrong.
